﴿By the Mount (al-Tur)﴾ He meant by it the mountain upon which Allah Most High spoke to Musa, peace be upon him, in the Holy Land. Allah Most High swore by it.

It was also said: it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz). It was also said: it is the registers of the recording angels, which will be brought out to them on the Day of Resurrection unrolled, so one will take his in his right hand and another will take his in his left. Its proof is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We will bring forth for him on the Day of Resurrection a record which he will find unrolled﴾ [al-Isra: 13].

﴿And the Frequented House (al-Bayt al-Ma'mur)﴾ because of the abundance of those who visit it and its inhabitants. It is a house in the heaven, opposite the Throne, in line with the Ka'bah, called al-Durah. Its sanctity in the heavens is like the sanctity of the Ka'bah on earth. ﴿And the Raised Canopy﴾ meaning: the heaven. Its parallel is the saying of the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And We made the heaven a protected canopy﴾ [al-Anbiya: 32].

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 52, verses 6–8:**

﴿And by the sea that is kindled﴾. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi and al-Dahhak said: it means the one that is set alight and heated, like the kindled oven (al-tannur al-masjur). This is also the view of Ibn Abbas. It is related that Allah, exalted is He, will make all the seas on the Day of Resurrection into fire, and it will be added to the Fire of Hell, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And when the seas are set boiling﴾ [al-Takwir: 6]. And there is a hadith from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "No man should ride the sea except for the purpose of raiding, performing 'umrah, or hajj, for beneath the sea is fire, and beneath the fire is sea."[[Related by Abu Dawud in al-Jihad, chapter on riding the sea (3/359), from Bishr ibn Muslim, from Abd Allah ibn Amr. He said: "There is irregularity (idtirab) in this hadith. It has been narrated from Bishr in this form, and it has also been narrated from him that it reached him from Abd Allah ibn Amr, and it has been narrated from him from a man, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, and other variants have been mentioned." Al-Bukhari mentioned it in his History and recorded this hadith, noting its irregularity, and said: "His hadith is not authentic." Al-Khattabi said: "They have declared the chain of this hadith weak." See: Silsilat al-Ahadith al-Da'ifah by al-Albani, no. 478.]]

Mujahid and al-Kalbi said: "al-Masjur" means "filled up," as one says: "I filled the vessel" (sajjartu al-ina' idha mala'tuhu).

Al-Hasan, Qatadah and Abu al-Aliyah said: it is the dry one whose water has gone and dried up.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: it is the one in which fresh water and salt water are mixed.

Al-Dahhak related from al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, from Ali, that he said concerning "the sea that is kindled": it is a sea beneath the Throne, its depth is like the distance between the seven heavens and the seven earths. In it is a thick water called the Sea of Life (bahr al-hayawan). After the first blast, it will rain upon the servants for forty mornings, and they will grow in their graves.[[Related by al-Tabari (27/20). al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (7/629) to Ibn Abi Hatim, Abd al-Razzaq and Sa'id ibn Mansur.]] This is the view of Muqatil: Allah swore by these things.

﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur﴾, i.e., it will descend and take place.

﴿There is none that can avert it﴾, i.e., none that can prevent it. Jubayr ibn Mut'im said: I came to Medina to speak with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the prisoners of Badr. I came to him while he was leading his Companions in the Maghrib prayer, and his voice was coming out of the mosque. I heard him recite "By the Mount (al-Tur)" up to his words: "Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is bound to occur; there is none that can avert it." My heart was nearly split when I heard it, and I had not yet embraced Islam at that time. He said: So I embraced Islam out of fear of the descent of the punishment, and I did not think I would rise from my place before the punishment would befall me.[[Related by al-Bukhari in the Tafsir, Tafsir of Surah al-Tur (8/603).]]

**Ma'alim al-Tanzil (Baghawi's Commentary) on Surah 52, verses 19–21:**

﴿Eat and drink with ease﴾, free from the fear of consequence, from indigestion and sickness, ﴿for what you used to do﴾.

﴿Reclining on couches arranged in rows﴾, placed side by side, ﴿and We will pair them with houris, with beautiful, wide eyes﴾.

﴿As for those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith﴾: Abu 'Amr recited "wa-atba'nahum" (and We caused them to follow), with an alif of exaltation (the first alif is elided in reading, using the form of the first person plural for exaltation), and "dhurriyyatihim" (their offspring), with an alif and a kasra on the ta' in both words, in accordance with His saying "alhaqna bihim" (We joined them) and "wa ma alatnahum" (We did not deprive them), so that the discourse follows one consistent pattern.

The others recited "wa-attaba'tahum" with a connected alif, a shadda on the ta' after it, and a sukun on the final ta'.

Then they differed regarding "dhurriyyatuhum" (their offspring). The people of Madina recited the first (word) [[Addition from manuscript "b".]] without an alif and with a damma on the ta', and the second with an alif and a kasra on the ta'. The people of Syria and Ya'qub recited both with an alif and a kasra on the ta' in the second. The others recited without an alif in both, with a raf' (damma) on the ta' in the first and a nasb (fatha) on it in the second.

They also differed regarding the meaning of the verse. Some said: its meaning is, "And those who believed, and whose offspring followed them in faith": that is, their children, both young and adult. The adults follow by their own faith, and the young by the faith of their fathers, since a young child is judged to be Muslim by following one of his two parents. ﴿We shall join with them their offspring﴾ who are believers [in Paradise according to their ranks, even if their deeds do not reach the ranks of their fathers] [[What is between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "a".]], as an honour to their fathers, so that their eyes may be comforted thereby. This is the narration of Sa'id ibn Jubayr from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both.

Others said: its meaning is, "And those who believed, and whose offspring who had reached maturity followed them in faith, We join with them their young offspring who had not reached the age of faith, by the faith of their fathers." This is the view of al-Dahhak, and the narration of al-'Awfi from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both. Allah, mighty and majestic, informs that He gathers for His believing servant his offspring in Paradise, just as he loved in this world that they should gather around him. He admits them to Paradise by His grace, and raises them to his rank through the deed of their father, without diminishing the fathers' deeds in any way. This is His saying: ﴿And We did not deprive them﴾ (Ibn Kathir read "alatahum" with a kasra on the lam; the rest read it with a fatha), that is, We did not reduce the fathers, ﴿of their deeds at all﴾.

﴿Eat and drink with ease﴾, free from the fear of consequence, from indigestion and sickness, ﴿for what you used to do﴾.

﴿Reclining on couches arranged in rows﴾, placed side by side, ﴿and We will pair them with houris, with beautiful, wide eyes﴾.

The others recited "wa-attaba'tahum" with a connected alif, a shadda on the ta' after it, and a sukun on the final ta'.

Then they differed regarding "dhurriyyatuhum" (their offspring). The people of Madina recited the first (word) [[Addition from manuscript "b".]] without an alif and with a damma on the ta', and the second with an alif and a kasra on the ta'. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verses 22–26:

﴿And We provided them with fruit﴾ in addition to what they already had, ﴿and meat of whatever they desire﴾ from all kinds of meat.

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ That is, they say that he fabricates the Qur'an of his own accord. Ibn Kaysan said: "Were they created in vain and left neglected (sudan), not commanded and not forbidden?" Muqatil said: "Do they hold the keys of your Lord through the message, so that they may place it wherever they wish?" She said: When he stood, he would say Allahu akbar ten times, and say Alhamdulillah ten times, and Subhan Allah ten times, and La ilaha illa Allah ten times, and Astaghfir Allah ten times, and he would say: "Allahumma ighfir li, wahdini, warzuqni, wa 'afini (O Allah, forgive me, guide me, provide for me, and grant me well-being)," and he would seek refuge from the constriction of the place (on the Day of Resurrection). [[Recorded by Abu Dawud in the Book of Prayer, chapter on what is said to open the prayer: 1/373; al-Nasa'i in the Book of Night Prayer, chapter on what is said to open the night prayer: 3/208–209; and Ibn Majah in the Book of Iqamah, chapter on what is reported regarding supplication when a man rises at night, no. 1356: 1/431.]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 52, verse 49:

﴿And glorify Him during the night﴾, that is, pray to Him. Muqatil said: this means the Maghrib and 'Isha' prayers.

﴿And at the setting of the stars﴾, meaning the two rak'ahs before the Fajr prayer, and that is when the stars set (tudbiru al-nujum, i.e., they disappear) by the light of dawn. This is the view of most of the exegetes. Al-Dahhak said: it refers to the obligatory Fajr prayer.
